title: Australia Black Summer

link.method: Pearson r of daily values: Sydney mean PM2.5 (NSW monitors) vs SE Australia daily total FRP (VIIRS), fires leading by 0 to 5 days
link.lag_search: lags 0..5 days, partner leading the hero only (negative lag = partner leads)

gaps: Fire points: all 507,028 VIIRS detections in south-east Australia (39-28S, 140-154E) in the window, merged into 29,059 flames (detections within 5 km on the same day become one flame at the place of their strongest detection, size = their summed FRP).

Flame size is linear in summed FRP up to 2586 MW (99th percentile); larger flames drawn at that size. Only nominal and high confidence vegetation fire detections; VIIRS passes about twice a day and thick smoke can hide fires.
Sydney PM2.5 = mean of the 15 Sydney monitors of the NSW network reporting PM2.5 each day (median 14 per day); daily values are 24 h means of local calendar days (AEST), aligned on the UTC story day.
Normal = Sydney monitors over the same window in the 2015-16, 2016-17, 2017-18, 2018-19 summers (4 seasons); the set of monitors grew over those years.

Canberra = ACT Health monitors (Civic, Florey, Monash), daily means of hourly PM2.5 (pm2_5_1_hr) on local days, only days with at least 18 hours; drawn as pillars but not part of the Sydney hero lane.

Smoke = GEOS-CF surface PM2.5 (a model with satellite data assimilated, not a measurement), daily mean of 8 three-hourly values, 0.25 deg; drawn linear from a floor of 15 to 150 ug/m3, higher values at full density. Particles move on GEOS-CF daily mean 10 m wind (1 deg).

Heat = GEOS-CF 2 m temperature (model) daily mean of 8 three-hourly values at 0.5 deg, drawn linear 10 to 40 deg C; daily means hide the afternoon peaks (for example the 48.9 deg C measured at Penrith on 4 January 2020).
1 day without any Sydney PM2.5 value stays empty.

The model smoke is much thicker over Sydney than measured (GEOS-CF peak daily mean 671 vs 107 ug/m3 at the monitors): use the smoke layer for where the smoke went, the pillars for how much people breathed.
The Sydney link is modest (r 0.301 at 4 days, r 0.184 same day): Sydney's smoke depended on wind direction more than on total fire power; Canberra, closer to the fires, links more clearly (r 0.571).
The link uses all 107 days; long smoky runs make consecutive days similar, so r is indicative, not a test.

hero_norm.method: daily mean PM2.5 over Sydney NSW monitors, same window (Nov 1 to Feb 15) of each baseline summer

sources.name: VIIRS S-NPP 375 m active fires (VNP14IMG), country yearly CSV
PM2.5 daily averages, Sydney monitoring network
GEOS-CF v1 assimilation, surface PM2.5 (pm25_rh35_gcc), 10 m wind, 2 m temperature
